heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Governor
text: Scott Jewett is a leader, entrepreneur, innovator, lifelong problem solver, and family man who calls Boca Raton home. Like so many Floridians, he and his wife Regina face the daily realities of homeownership, rising insurance costs , and the desire to leave a freer, more prosperous state to the next generation.

heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Governor
text: He is running for Governor because he believes Florida can do better , with less government overreach, more individual liberty, and practical solutions that put people first.

heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Governor
text: His agenda centers on a robust economy with more living wage jobs , real educational choice, public safety, lower taxes, and a government that respects the rights of every Floridian, regardless of which major party they usually vote for.

heading: Fighting for Families in Florida
text: Floridians are feeling the squeeze every month . Insurance premiums keep climbing, everyday costs keep rising, and too much of your hard earned money disappears into government waste. Scott Jewett is fighting to fix the insurance affordability crisis, cut taxes, shrink the size of government, and put real solutions in place that help families keep more of what they earn. He believes Florida can do better when we put people first .

heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Lieutenant Governor
text: Nicole Skelly lives in Milton, Florida with her husband and their two children. Together they have owned and run a construction business for many years.

heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Lieutenant Governor
text: As a small business owner and mom, Nicole knows the daily pressure of rising costs, heavy rules, and government overreach . She believes parents and hardworking families should be trusted more than bureaucrats.

heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Lieutenant Governor
text: Nicole is ready to help cut the red tape that drives up prices, protect parental rights , and fight for a Florida where people can keep more of what they earn and live free. She wants her kids, and every Florida family, to have the same chance that hard work should still provide.

heading: Volunteer
text: Join the team that’s fighting for liberty in Florida. Help us knock doors, make calls, and spread the message that real change is possible. Every hour counts.

heading: Stay Informed
text: Get campaign updates, event invites, and policy news delivered straight to your inbox. Stay connected and never miss a chance to make your voice heard.

heading: Register to Vote
text: Your vote is your power. Confirm you’re registered and ready to support liberty at the ballot box. Florida’s future depends on it.

heading: Major Donors
text: Ready to make a major impact? Join the supporters fueling a serious challenge to the status quo and help put liberty back on the ballot.

heading: Answers to common questions.
text: Here you’ll find clear, straightforward answers to the questions we hear most often from Floridians. If you don’t see your question listed, feel free to reach out; we’re happy to communicate with everyone, you voices matter.

heading: Answers to common questions.
text: Check out the frequently asked questions page for more questions and answers.

heading: How will you actually lower my homeowners insurance premiums?
text: Government rules and state programs keep pushing your insurance higher. We will cut those rules and open the market so more companies compete for your business. More competition means lower premiums for Florida homeowners.

heading: How are you different from the other candidates?
text: We're not part of the two big parties that keep raising costs and taking more control. I trust parents, workers, and small business owners more than government. Most Floridians already live this way; they just want to be left alone. That’s the real difference.

heading: What’s your plan to reduce the overall cost of living in Florida; groceries, housing, insurance, and utilities?
text: Cut the rules and taxes that drive prices up. Open markets so more companies compete on groceries, housing, insurance, and power. When government gets out of the way, costs fall for working Florida families.

heading: What’s your position on school choice and making sure parents have real options for their kids’ education?
text: Parents should decide where their kids go to school. We support real school choice so education dollars follow the child, not the system. Public, private, charter, or homeschool, families pick what works best. Bureaucrats don’t.

heading: News
text: Read the latest campaign news, press releases, and media coverage as Scott and Nicole take the message of liberty across Florida.

heading: Videos
text: Watch speeches, interviews, and campaign videos. Hear directly from Scott and Nicole on the issues that matter most to Floridians.

heading: Social Media
text: Follow the campaign for real-time updates, live events, and conversations. Join the growing movement for liberty in Florida.

text: Be part of the grassroots movement that is representing all Floridians!

heading: Florida families are paying more and getting less
text: Florida does not have one money problem. It has a stack of them . Insurance. Taxes. Housing. Power bills. Healthcare. Government growth. They all land on the same kitchen table.

heading: Florida families are paying more and getting less
text: Scott Jewett and Nicole Skelly trust you. You know how to raise your kids, run your shop, and take care of your family. You should keep more of what you earn . You should live free.

heading: Florida families are paying more and getting less
text: Scroll down to get more information about where we stand on the issues and what we plan to do. You can also click on one of the issues from the list to go directly to that issue .

heading: Stop the Squeeze on Florida Families
text: We have an affordability crisis. Groceries, housing, homeowners insurance, property taxes, utilities, gas, car insurance, car payments, health insurance, childcare, and eating out are more expensive now. Utilities keep climbing. Parents pick up extra hours. Gig workers drive later. Small shops stay open longer and still fall behind.

heading: Stop the Squeeze on Florida Families
text: Government did not feel that squeeze first. Families did. When Tallahassee or Washington adds a rule, a fee, or a new program, the cost shows up in the price of milk, the rent check, and the mortgage payment on a modest home.

heading: Stop the Squeeze on Florida Families
text: Floridians are not asking for a lecture about the economy. They are asking why they work harder and keep less.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Hardworking people should keep more of what they earn. Government should get out of the way so prices can come down and paychecks can stretch further.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Cost of living is not one bill. It is insurance, property taxes, housing, energy, healthcare, and red tape stacked on the same family. Fix those pressures and everyday life gets cheaper.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: We trust Floridians to run their own budgets . Government should have to live on one too.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Treat cost of living as the test for every state decision: does this make life cheaper for families, or more expensive?

heading: What We Will Do
text: Cut rules and fees that raise the price of food, housing, energy, insurance, and hiring.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Stop shifting government costs onto household bills.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Force agencies to show how new rules hit parents, retirees, renters, and small shops before those rules take effect.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Tie the rest of this agenda together — insurance, taxes, housing, healthcare, energy, and spending — so the kitchen table squeeze actually eases.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Florida families should not have to work two jobs to afford one life. Keep what you earn. Live free.

heading: Fix the Insurance Affordability Crisis
text: Florida homeowners pay some of the highest premiums in the country . When the roof leaks or the storm hits, too little of that money comes back to fix the house.

heading: Fix the Insurance Affordability Crisis
text: Retirees on fixed incomes open a renewal letter and wonder if they can stay. Young families trying to buy a first home get priced out before they ever unpack. Small landlords raise rent because the premium jumped again. Coastal towns watch private insurers leave, then watch Citizens grow.

heading: Fix the Insurance Affordability Crisis
text: The system is broken by waste, lawsuits that do not help homeowners, rules that chase companies out, and claims practices that grind families down. Storm risk is real. The bloated system on top of that risk is a choice.

heading: Fix the Insurance Affordability Crisis
text: Floridians are not asking for another press conference. They are asking why they pay six times more in premiums than they ever see paid out in claims.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Insurance should protect the home, not feed a bloated system . Premiums should be honest. Claims should get paid. Families should not be trapped with one expensive option.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Homeowners deserve competition, clear rules, and a market that wants to write coverage in Florida . Citizens should be a safety net, not the default company for half the state.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Scott has already drafted insurance reform work because he refuses to accept that this is “just Florida.” People who pay the bill deserve a system that works when they need it.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Cut the waste that drives premiums up and keeps claim dollars from reaching damaged homes.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Increase competition so more companies want to insure Florida families.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Protect homeowners from abusive claims practices and endless runaround.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Keep Citizens as a backstop, not a growing substitute for a working market.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Tell families the truth about flood risk and storm exposure instead of hiding costs until renewal day.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Measure reform the only way that matters: are premiums coming down, and do claims get paid?

heading: What We Will Do
text: Your home should not be a luxury item because the insurance system failed. Fix the insurance affordability crisis.

heading: Stop Taxing People Out of Their Homes
text: You worked a lifetime to own your house. Then the county sends another bill for the privilege of living in it. If the value on paper goes up, the tax can go up even when your paycheck does not.

heading: Stop Taxing People Out of Their Homes
text: That hits retirees on fixed incomes first. It hits widows who want to stay on the same street. It hits young families who finally bought a starter home and then learned the tax bill is another mortgage.

heading: Stop Taxing People Out of Their Homes
text: Parents should not have to choose between keeping the house and paying for groceries. Small shops tied to a building feel the same squeeze. Local government got used to spending the increase. Families got used to being told there is no other way.

heading: Stop Taxing People Out of Their Homes
text: There is another way. If you own your home, you should not keep paying rent to the government forever.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Eliminate 100% of property taxes on homesteaded homes . Your home, your money, and your freedom belong to you, not them.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Florida families should never be taxed out of houses they already paid for . Government should live within its means, just like those families do.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Property tax relief is not a gift . It is the state admitting it does not own your house.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Fight to eliminate homestead property taxes so owners are not billed every year for staying in their own home.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Force state and local governments to set priorities and cut waste instead of leaning on the next assessment increase.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Protect retirees and fixed income owners who did everything right and still fear the tax notice.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Be honest that government will have to spend less. That is the point. Families already do.

heading: What We Will Do
text: If you own your home, you shouldn’t have to keep paying the government for the privilege of living in it.

heading: Florida Housing Should Not Be So Expensive
text: A young couple wants a starter home near work. The listing is gone in a weekend, or the payment is impossible once insurance and taxes land on top of the mortgage . A teacher rents farther from school each year. A restaurant crew drives an hour because nothing nearby is open at their wage.

heading: Florida Housing Should Not Be So Expensive
text: That is not only a market story. Rules, delays, and layered approvals make it slower and more expensive to build the homes working people need. When government makes building hard, families pay rent for the delay.

heading: Florida Housing Should Not Be So Expensive
text: Longtime residents get pushed out of the neighborhoods they helped build . Adult children cannot move back near their parents. Small landlords sell because insurance and taxes ate the margin. “Affordable housing” becomes a slogan while the starter home disappears.

heading: Florida Housing Should Not Be So Expensive
text: Floridians should not have to leave Florida to afford Florida.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Housing gets cheaper when people are free to build, buy, and rent without a maze of permission . Get government out of the way of new homes, especially starter homes.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Property rights matter . So does the ability of working people to live near the jobs that keep this state running.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: We will not pretend a new office in Tallahassee can wish prices down . Cut the barriers.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Strip the red tape that makes ordinary homes take years and extra dollars to approve.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Support local decisions that add starter homes and rentals without turning every project into a political fight.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Stop stacking insurance, tax, and fee costs onto the monthly payment until working families are priced out.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Respect property rights while rejecting the idea that government should pick winners among developers.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Measure success by whether nurses, teachers, tradespeople, and young families can still live in their communities.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Florida should be a place you can start a life, not a place you get priced out of.

heading: Secure Borders. Legal Opportunity.
text: A free country should welcome peaceful people who come here to work, build a life, and join a community . Freedom also depends on knowing who is coming in.

heading: Secure Borders. Legal Opportunity.
text: When the system is slow, confusing, and unfair, honest people wait in line while criminals, traffickers, and cartels look for gaps . That is not compassion. That is a broken process that hurts citizens, legal immigrants, workers, and business owners.

heading: Secure Borders. Legal Opportunity.
text: Florida families feel it in crowded services, strained schools, and job sites where the rules seem to apply to some people and not others . Small business owners who follow the law watch competitors who do not. Communities want order, not chaos and not cruelty.

heading: Secure Borders. Legal Opportunity.
text: The two major parties use this issue to raise money and pick a fight . Floridians want a system that is lawful, faster for honest people, and tough on people who hurt others.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Secure the border. Make legal immigration simpler and faster . Focus enforcement on criminals, traffickers, and real security threats.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Peaceful people who want to work and follow the law should not face a wall of bureaucracy . People who commit crimes should not get a pass.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: The goal is more freedom, less bureaucracy , and a system that is fair to citizens, immigrants, workers, and businesses alike.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Support secure borders and clear enforcement against criminals, traffickers, and genuine security threats.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Push for a simpler, faster legal path so honest people can come, work, and contribute without disappearing into a backlog.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Stop using Floridians as props in a national shouting match.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Protect the rule of law so legal residents and citizens are not asked to ignore the rules everyone else is told to follow.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Judge policy by whether communities are safer and whether peaceful workers have a lawful way in.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Welcome people who come to build a life and assimilate. Stop people who come to harm our way of life. Make the lawful path the easier path.

heading: Parents Should Decide
text: Parents know their children better than any official in Tallahassee. They know how their kid learns. They know when a school is working and when it is not.

heading: Parents Should Decide
text: Too often the system protects itself first . Families get assigned a building and told to be grateful. Teachers get buried in paperwork. Kids who need something different wait. A mom who wants to homeschool, pick a charter, or try a small private school should not have to fight the state for permission to do what is best for her child.

heading: Parents Should Decide
text: Young people starting out need skills that lead to work , not a pile of debt and a diploma that does not open a door. Higher education should serve students, not a bureaucracy.

heading: Parents Should Decide
text: Education is not a turf war between politicians . It is a parent standing in a doorway asking, “Will this help my kid?”

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Parents decide. Funding should follow the student , whether that is a traditional public school, a charter, a private school, homeschool, or another option that fits the child.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: ZIP code and income should not trap a family in a school that is failing their kid . Choice is for every parent, not only the ones who can already buy their way out.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Education should help children succeed. It should not exist to protect a government system.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Put parents in the driver’s seat and keep them there.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Make money follow the child so families have real options, not just a brochure.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Cut the rules that bury teachers in paperwork and pull time away from students.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Keep curriculum decisions close to families. No identity politics in the classroom. Teach kids. Don’t recruit them.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Demand results from schools and colleges that take public money. If it does not help students, it does not get a blank check.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Parents, not bureaucrats, should make the big choices for their kids.

heading: Care You Can Afford. Choices You Can Use.
text: Healthcare is personal. It is the nurse on a long shift who still cannot afford her own bill. It is the family opening a surprise statement after a short ER visit. It is the worker who loses a job and suddenly wonders if the medicine stays available.

heading: Care You Can Afford. Choices You Can Use.
text: This year, hundreds of thousands of Floridians lost subsidized coverage or saw prices jump. People did not become less sick. The paperwork and the price tag changed.

heading: Care You Can Afford. Choices You Can Use.
text: Government keeps adding rules that sound helpful and then show up as higher premiums, narrower networks, and fewer choices . Small business owners trying to cover a crew feel it. Gig workers who buy their own plan feel it. Retirees stuck between systems feel it.

heading: Care You Can Afford. Choices You Can Use.
text: Families do not need another slogan. They need a doctor they can see and a bill they can pay.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Patients and healthcare professionals should come first. People need affordable care and more choices, not a thicker rulebook.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Government should not make healthcare more expensive or more confusing . More options, clearer prices, and fewer barriers beat another layer of control.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: A nurse or doctor should be free to care for patients. A family should be free to pick the coverage that fits their life.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Fight rules that raise premiums and shrink the number of plans families can actually use.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Push for clearer prices so a parent can know the cost before the bill arrives.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Expand choices for workers, small shops, and people who buy coverage on their own.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Keep the focus on patients and the people who treat them, not on protecting a system.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Tell the truth when federal subsidy changes hit Florida households, and refuse to pretend Tallahassee can hide the cost.

heading: What We Will Do
text: People need care they can reach and a price they can live with. Government should stop making that harder.

heading: Grow Without Crushing Communities
text: Florida is growing because people want to be here. That should be good news. Too often it feels like a traffic jam, a crowded classroom, and a construction fence where a familiar view used to be.

heading: Grow Without Crushing Communities
text: Parents spend half the afternoon in the car. Truck drivers lose hours on the same stretch of road. Homeowners watch a wetland or a tree line vanish and then get told the pipes and schools will “catch up later.” Later usually means another fee.

heading: Grow Without Crushing Communities
text: Growth without capacity is how you get angry neighborhoods and brittle systems . Growth with a pile of special deals is how you get the feeling that someone else got the break.

heading: Grow Without Crushing Communities
text: People are not against the next family moving in. They are against a government that approves the rooftops and forgets the roads, water, and schools those rooftops need.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Communities should grow without being crushed . Infrastructure is not a favor. If you allow the houses, you have to be honest about the roads, water, sewer, and classrooms.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Local people and property owners should have a real voice . Distant agencies and sweetheart incentives should not run the map.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Florida can welcome people and still protect the places that make this state worth living in.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Demand that roads, water, sewer, and schools keep up with growth instead of trailing it by a decade.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Cut the delays that raise costs, then dump those costs on the next buyer.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Stop using taxpayer incentives to force growth the community cannot support.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Respect property rights and local voices when a project changes a neighborhood.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Be honest about tradeoffs. Growth is not free. Neither is pretending the pipes will appear on their own.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Florida can grow and still feel like home. The roads, water, and schools have to keep up, and the special deals have to stop.

heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
text: A family that just finished boarding the windows should not also be praying the insurance company picks up the phone . A fisherman knows the water. A farmer knows the land. A homeowner on a canal knows what happens when the surge comes.

heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
text: Florida lives with storms. That will not change. What can change is whether we keep building the next neighborhood in the next vulnerable place, then acting surprised when the bill arrives. Water quality, the Everglades, and coastal flooding are not abstract “environment” talk. They are drinking water, jobs, and whether the house is still standing.

heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
text: FAU polling found most Floridians worry about stronger storms and worse surge. They are right to. Risk is real. Hiding it until premium day is how families get trapped.

heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
text: Good stewards already live here . They do not need a lecture from a distant agency.

heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
text: They need honest rules, working mitigation , and a government that does not make recovery harder than the storm.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Farmers, fishermen, and homeowners care for the land they live on . Good stewards, not distant agencies, should make the big decisions about their own property.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Protecting water and coast is how you protect homes, jobs, and the next generation’s Florida . Property rights and clean water are not opposites.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Storm readiness and insurance costs are the same conversation . Pretending otherwise is how premiums explode after the season ends.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Support preparedness and mitigation that actually protect homes and businesses, not just press releases after landfall.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Be honest about flood and surge risk so families are not sold a house the system cannot insure.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Protect water quality and the Everglades without burying working people in paperwork that does not clean a single gallon.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Respect property rights. Stop treating every owner like the problem.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Connect storm policy to insurance reform so recovery does not become a second disaster.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Protect the home. Protect the water. Trust the people who live on the land to be good stewards of it.

heading: Government Should Live on a Budget
text: When a family earns less, they cut what they cannot afford . When a small shop has a bad month, the owner skips a draw and watches every receipt. Government does the opposite. It asks for more.

heading: Government Should Live on a Budget
text: Floridians see waste and then get told the answer is another tax, another fee, another program . Retirees who saved carefully watch Tallahassee spend like the well never runs dry. Parents who pack lunches watch agencies grow.

heading: Government Should Live on a Budget
text: Rules pile up. So do hidden costs. A new form does not look like a tax . It still takes a Saturday the shop owner does not have. A camera network does not look like a tax. It still treats free people like suspects for driving to work.

heading: Government Should Live on a Budget
text: Accountability is not a slogan. It is whether anyone can follow the money and say no.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: It is your money . Government should spend it only when the expense is truly necessary.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Lower taxes and tighter budgets force government to set priorities, cut waste, and become accountable. That is how families already live.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Transparency is not optional . Free people have a right to see how they are being governed — and a right not to be tracked just for using the road.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Demand that government live on a budget the way families and small shops already do.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Cut waste before asking taxpayers for another dollar.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Shrink the rulebook that costs time and money without making life safer or better.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Open the books. If the public cannot see it, it should not be spent.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Oppose warrantless tracking of everyday Floridians, including ALPR and Flock style camera networks that log parents, nurses, and delivery drivers.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Stop asking taxpayers for more. Start making government do more with what it already has.

heading: Keep Communities Safe. Protect Your Rights.
text: A store owner should not dread the next smash and grab . A parent should not change the walk to school. A senior living alone should not feel like the easy target. Nurses leaving a night shift should get to the car in peace. "Teen Take Overs" are not an acceptable trend.

heading: Keep Communities Safe. Protect Your Rights.
text: Florida communities need to be safe . That means going after people who hurt others: violent offenders, traffickers, dealers who poison neighborhoods, and crews that treat theft like a business.

heading: Keep Communities Safe. Protect Your Rights.
text: It also means the justice system should spend its time on real threats, not on turning everyday life into a dragnet . Warrantless cameras that log every errand do not make a family safer. They treat free people like suspects.

heading: Keep Communities Safe. Protect Your Rights.
text: Law abiding parents and homeowners have the right to protect their families . Public safety and constitutional rights are not a trade. A free state can do both.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Keep communities safe . Give law enforcement the tools to go after violent crime, trafficking, drugs, and organized theft.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Demand accountability . Focus the justice system on people who pose a real threat. Protect the rights of everyone else.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Free people should not have their every move recorded for driving down the road . This campaign opposes ALPR camera networks and mass surveillance of lawful residents.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Law abiding Floridians have the right to keep and bear arms to protect their homes and families . That right should not be chipped away by politicians who do not trust the people.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Support effective policing aimed at violent crime, trafficking, drugs, and organized theft.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Push courts and prosecutors to focus resources on people who threaten public safety.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Protect constitutional rights, including due process and the right of law abiding people to defend themselves.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Reject mass surveillance of everyday travel, including Flock style ALPR systems.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Give local law enforcement flexibility to solve problems in their own communities, and hold them accountable when they abuse that power.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Safe streets. Free people. Go after real threats. Leave law abiding Floridians alone.

heading: Get Government Out of the Way of Work
text: Nicole and her husband have made payroll since 2007. They know what a new rule from Tallahassee does to a small carpentry shop . It does not hit the politician first. It hits the owner who cannot pass the cost on and the crew that needs hours next week.

heading: Get Government Out of the Way of Work
text: Gig workers picking up weekend rides, parents running a side hustle from the kitchen table, and young people trying to start something all run into the same wall : permits, licenses, and delays that have nothing to do with serving a customer.

heading: Get Government Out of the Way of Work
text: Florida can attract new industries . It can also scare them off with taxes, power bill surprises, and a rulebook that only the big players can afford to read. Workers do not need a slogan about jobs. They need an employer who can afford to hire them.

heading: Get Government Out of the Way of Work
text: A robust economy with more living wage work is how families stay . Government does not create that by adding another office. It creates that by getting out of the way.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Trust people who build things . Small shops, the self employed, and gig workers should be free to earn a living without asking permission for every step.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Keep taxes competitive. Cut rules that make it expensive to hire. Welcome new industries without handing them a taxpayer subsidy.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Scott has built companies and solved hard problems in the private sector . Nicole has kept a family business alive through good years and bad ones. That is the economy they will fight for.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Cut occupational licenses and rules that block people from working.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Make it cheaper and simpler to hire, especially for small shops. Keep Florida competitive on taxes without selling the state off through special deals.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Support workforce paths that lead to real jobs, trades, skills, and new industries, instead of paperwork theaters.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Say no to barriers that protect connected companies and punish the next startup.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Let Floridians work, hire, and build. The best jobs plan is less permission and more freedom.

heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
text: A potential simple solution: The data center provides its own power, uses an internal heat exchange cooling system similar to a car radiator, and is not built near neighborhoods or cities. This way they don't use existing power grids or existing water supplies.

heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
text: A retiree on a fixed income should not see the power bill jump because a warehouse of computers moved in down the road. A small shop should not subsidize the water and substations of a company that could write a check.

heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
text: Artificial intelligence is bringing real investment. That can mean jobs and better tools. It can also mean massive data centers that gulp electricity, water, and land.

heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
text: When government hands out incentives and then quietly socializes the infrastructure, ordinary Floridians pick up the tab .

heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
text: Neighbors worry about wells, wetlands , and whether the next rate case will treat a tech campus like just another customer. Property owners worry about eminent domain dressed up as “economic development.” Parents wonder why their light bill is part of someone else’s business plan.

heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
text: Florida should not be for sale. Innovation is welcome. A hidden tax on households is not.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Welcome technological investment . Do not force residents and small businesses to subsidize it.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Data centers should pay their own way for power, water, land, and grid upgrades . Taxpayers should not underwrite some of the world’s largest technology companies.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Energy policy should serve Florida families first . That includes cleaner, safer, reliable power, and it includes nuclear as part of a serious energy future.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Property rights and local voices come before ribbon cuttings.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Require data centers and similar projects to cover the power, water, and infrastructure they use instead of shifting costs onto household rates.

heading: What We Will Do
text: End taxpayer incentives that socialize the downside and privatize the upside for giant tech firms.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Protect property rights and water resources when a project changes a community.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Plan energy capacity for Florida homes and shops first, then for industrial demand that pays its own bill.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Support cleaner, safer, reliable energy, including nuclear, so the state is not stuck choosing between growth and brownouts.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Florida should welcome builders and innovators. It should not put their power bill on your kitchen table.

heading: Your Drive Home Is Not a Government File
text: Flock cameras do not just look for criminals . They quietly track everyday Floridians. A parent driving kids to school. A nurse heading to a night shift. A small business owner making deliveries. A retiree going to the store. The camera does not care why you were on that road. It logs you anyway.

heading: Your Drive Home Is Not a Government File
text: Once that data is collected, it can be searched and shared . Often without a warrant. Often without you ever knowing. A system built to catch a stolen car becomes a system that can reconstruct your week.

heading: Your Drive Home Is Not a Government File
text: That is not how free people should live. You should be able to drive home without becoming a line in a government file. Safety does not require treating every law abiding driver like a suspect.

heading: Your Drive Home Is Not a Government File
text: Communities still need real policing aimed at real threats. Tracking every errand is not the same thing. It is cheaper for government to watch everyone than to do the harder work of going after people who actually hurt others.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Free people should not have their every move recorded by the government just for driving down the road.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: This campaign is against Flock cameras. It is against ALPR networks. It is against warrantless mass tracking of lawful residents.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: If police have a suspect and a warrant, they can do their job. That is a far cry from logging parents, nurses, and delivery drivers by default.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Your life is your business. Getting to work is not probable cause.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Oppose Flock cameras and all ALPR systems that scan and store the movements of everyday Floridians.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Fight the spread of these networks in cities, counties, and along Florida roads.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Demand a warrant before government searches travel data that can rebuild a person’s day.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Stop selling “public safety” as a reason to watch people who have done nothing wrong.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Keep law enforcement focused on violent crime, trafficking, and real threats, not on building a map of every drive to school and every night shift.

heading: What We Will Do
text: You should be able to drive your kids to school without the government keeping the receipt. We are against Flock cameras. Period.

heading: Parents Have the Right to Protect Their Families
text: A law abiding parent should not have to ask permission to protect their kids . A homeowner should not have to hope the sheriff arrives in time. A woman closing a shop at night should not be told her right to defend herself is a talking point for later.

heading: Parents Have the Right to Protect Their Families
text: Politicians who do not trust the people keep chipping away at that right . Another rule. Another list. Another delay. None of it stops a criminal who already ignores the law. It does land on the nurse, the truck driver, and the retiree who followed every rule and still gets treated like the problem.

heading: Parents Have the Right to Protect Their Families
text: Florida families live in the real world. They lock the doors . They walk a dark parking lot. They want their children safe. The Second Amendment was written for those people, not for a committee in Tallahassee.

heading: Parents Have the Right to Protect Their Families
text: Scott and Nicole trust you with your own life . That includes the tools you use to protect it.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Law abiding parents and homeowners have the right to protect their families . That right should not be chipped away by politicians who do not trust the people.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: This campaign is pro Second Amendment. No half measures . Support the right to possess, carry, and modify weapons and accessories for self defense and to keep a free people free.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: We support open carry and constitutional carry in Florida . We oppose restrictions on weapons, ammunition, and accessories, unless a private property owner sets those rules on their own premises.

heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
text: Private property still belongs to the owner. Your rights do not stop at the state line, and they do not disappear because someone in office got nervous.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Defend the right of law abiding Floridians to keep and bear arms without a new stack of permission slips.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Support constitutional carry and open carry in Florida. Oppose new restrictions on weapons, ammunition, and accessories.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Respect the right of private property owners to set rules on their own premises, and stop government from setting those rules for everyone else.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Reject the idea that trusting free people is dangerous, and that trusting politicians with a monopoly on force is safe.

heading: What We Will Do
text: Keep the focus on criminals who use guns to hurt people, not on parents and homeowners who keep one to stay alive.

heading: LIBERTARIAN PARTY OF FLORIDA PLATFORM
text: As proposed by the Platform Committee for the Libertarian Party of Florida Annual Business Meeting of February 26th, 2022

heading: LIBERTARIAN PARTY OF FLORIDA PLATFORM
text: Platform Committee Members: Chris Rose II, Chair Omar Recuero, Vice Chair Thomas Knapp Jonathan Loesche Josh Hlavka (ex-officio)

heading: LIBERTARIAN PARTY OF FLORIDA PLATFORM
text: STATEMENT OF PRINCIPLE We, the Libertarian Party of Florida, oppose the initiation of force to achieve political or social goals.

heading: LIBERTARIAN PARTY OF FLORIDA PLATFORM
text: PREAMBLE We, the Libertarian Party of Florida, stand for freedom and prosperity in our State based on the principles of personal responsibility and individual liberty. We challenge the cult of the omnipotent State in order to defend and promote liberty, whereby mankind may best prosper. Libertarians seek a society built on the pillars of individual liberty and equality under the law—a society in which all individuals are sovereign over their own lives. This most desirable method of organizing society is the natural order that arises when the inalienable rights of individuals to life, liberty, and property ownership are respected and protected.

heading: LIBERTARIAN PARTY OF FLORIDA PLATFORM
text: Individuals must be free to pursue their own interests and pleasures so long as their efforts do not involve the use of force or fraud, or violate the natural rights of others. Libertarians welcome the peace, prosperity, and diversity that freedom brings.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: In the absence of a declaration of war by the United States Congress, we oppose deployment of federal troops on Florida soil, except to defend our State in the event of foreign attack. We oppose sending Florida National Guard troops overseas. We call for restoring gubernatorial approval for the President to activate a State National Guard.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We support the unfettered ability to possess, carry, and modify weapons and accessories for purposes including but not limited to self defense and to secure the rights of the free individual. We support open carry and constitutional carry initiatives in Florida. We oppose all restrictions on weapons, ammunition and accessories, unless mandated by private property owners on their premises.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: 3. Undelegated Powers Belong to the States or the People

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We support the Tenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, which reserves to the States and the people thereof all powers not expressly delegated to the federal government, nor prohibited to the States elsewhere in the Constitution. We urge the Supreme Court to overturn Wickard v. Filburn, as this act is used to nullify the Tenth Amendment by expanding federal regulatory powers over the States.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We support equality under the law and condemn any law that either rewards or punishes any individual based on race, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other group identification. Each person has the same inalienable rights. It is the State’s duty to protect those rights for everyone equally.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We recognize private property rights as an extension of self ownership, the most basic human right. One of the functions of government is to protect the rights of all people in its jurisdiction. This includes private entities having the right to voluntarily transfer ownership of their private property free of government price or quantity controls, intervention, or taxation.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We support a systematic review and sunsetting of laws, regulations, and administrative guidance that do not meet the stated intent of the of the elected officials at the time of writing.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: Agents of the State should not be above the law. We advocate ending the immunity of all government officials, employees, and departments, from suits for compensatory damages. We oppose caps on restitution payments. We support the Florida Whistleblower Act and the Florida False Claims Act.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We support transparency and believe that Sunshine laws should apply to all public employees wherever and however they meet. All meetings and minutes must be readily available to the public and recording devices should be welcomed. There should be no laws prohibiting or limiting electronic recording devices and reporting of any public official, including law enforcement, while performing their duties.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We oppose the participation by the State of Florida in the federal Real ID Act and similar federal identification or database mandates designed to collect or share data on individuals not accused of crime.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We believe in the right to privacy for all peaceful individuals and condemn any attempts to subvert this right. Detaining, searching, or seizing persons or their property should always require a warrant from a State or Federal court based on probable cause of a crime being committed.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: Government should never protect, maintain, nor regulate the legal monopoly status of any corporation whether public or private, or of those corporations' ownership of any company or business. These actions create an unfair playing field and are beyond the scope of small and limited government. We believe all services, especially utilities, should operate in a free and highly competitive market, whereby benefit to the consumer is raised and costs are lowered.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We call for an end to federal spending on grants to States and local governments, coupled with an equal reduction of federal taxes. All public projects should be funded locally. Persons living and working in Florida should not be responsible financially for non federal services to citizens in a different State.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We believe marriage is a private contract between consenting adults. As such, government need not be involved in authentication, documentation, or limitation of the institution. We support abolishing licensing requirements and restrictions, recognizing these as undue burdens upon individuals and their personal lives. We favor written and witnessed prenuptial agreements to determine the dissolution process in the event of death or desired separation.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: There shall be no restrictions to the organization and mobilization of the population. This includes unrestricted ability by the whole of the people to obtain weapons, training, or supplies to defend the territory of Florida in order to secure a free and prosperous future for Floridians.

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: 15. Immigration Law Enforcement By State and Local Governments

heading: I. STATE GOVERNMENT
text: We oppose all policies or programs that enlist State and local government employees to enforce federal immigration laws or that require local and State authorities to comply with federal immigration law enforcement.

heading: II. ELECTIONS
text: 1. State Regulation of Political Parties

heading: II. ELECTIONS
text: The only electoral duty of the State government should be providing for fair and efficient conduct of elections. Political parties, like any private voluntary group, should be free from government control and allowed to establish their own rules for nomination procedures and conventions.

heading: II. ELECTIONS
text: We support Ranked Choice. We oppose Top Two primaries as this disproportionately suppresses minor political party representation in the general election. We also support including the option of None Of The Above (NOTA) on all ballots. In the event that NOTA receives a plurality of votes in any election, a new election should be held for which none of the losing candidates shall be eligible.

heading: II. ELECTIONS
text: We recognize current campaign finance laws as threats to free speech and association. We support a structure for candidates to voluntarily disclose campaign contributions. We advocate the acceptance of alternative monetary donations such as crypto currencies as campaign contributions. We also call for the repeal of caps on contributions to candidates and parties. We support amending campaign finance laws to require all candidates and political parties to provide for their own expenses with no taxpayer funding.

heading: II. ELECTIONS
text: We support open ballot access for all parties and individuals who wish to hold public office. There must be no barriers to entry for prospective political parties and candidates, including unattainable signature requirements, exorbitant fees, or other measures which limit ballot access to a political duarchy. In addition, Section 99.103 of Florida laws, which refunds 95% of the 3% candidate filing fees only to parties with a voter registration at or above 5% of the total, should be repealed.

heading: III. Courts
text: We support and encourage private adjudication of disputes by mutually acceptable arbitrators or mediators prior to utilizing the public court system. Current law unnecessarily constrains private adjudication as a first resort.

heading: III. Courts
text: The right of trial by jury must be respected in all criminal and civil cases. We support the right of jurors to (a) take notes during trials, (b) submit written questions to witnesses and the judge, (c) be provided with the judge’s instructions in writing, and (d) discuss evidence among themselves at any time.

heading: III. Courts
text: We support the right of defendants to a fully informed jury, which requires judges to instruct jurors of their authority to judge not only the facts, but also the justice of the law according to their own consciences. If a jury of peers deems a law unjust, oppressive, or inappropriately applied, it has the right and duty to acquit the defendant.

heading: III. Courts
text: We support restitution for victims of crimes or civil infractions at the expense of the perpetrators. Victims must also enjoy respect for their right to require the prosecutor to drop charges before a trial, or pardon the perpetrator after a conviction (without necessarily foregoing restitution), provided the victim is not threatened or coerced.

heading: III. Courts
text: No fault divorce laws are preferable to divorce laws that require assignment of fault. For mandatory personal injury insurance we oppose no fault laws and support requiring the insurance company of the driver at fault in an accident to pay any damages due those affected.

heading: III. Courts
text: We condemn seizure of assets other than for purposes of restitution after conviction of a crime as a violation of private property rights and due process. We urge our legislators to join with other States in abolishing civil asset forfeiture and pre conviction criminal asset forfeiture.

heading: III. Courts
text: We support equal treatment and oppose sexual discrimination in any judicial proceeding adjudicating a parental right, privilege or obligation concerning his or her child.

heading: III. Courts
text: The Bar Association must cease to be the official Florida organization to which all attorneys must belong. The legal profession must be opened to competition; its clients and purely private organizations should be the judges of the quality of attorney services.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: Law enforcement cannot guarantee individual safety. As such, we advocate that law enforcement is not the first line of defense for individual safety, but a second line of defense intended to render assistance to those requiring it. Self protection is a personal responsibility. Individuals have the right to defend themselves and to possess the means to do so. Decreasing the self reliance of the citizenry leads to an overemphasis of policing and an increased segregation of law enforcement personnel from the people they are paid to protect. Those in law enforcement are not above the community, but members of it.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: As such, we call for the removal of qualified immunity from all agents of law enforcement.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: We support the separation of federal military units from law enforcement and disaster relief. Local agencies should not accept weapons, equipment, nor training from the federal military.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: We call for ending the use of dogs by law enforcement; this abusive practice violates the right to privacy by performing unwarranted and unaccountable searches, and often serves to escalate conflict.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: State prison facilities must only be used for the incarceration of individuals who have violated the natural rights of other people. Non violent criminals should not be housed at the expense of the public. Instead, non violent criminals should be kept on parole, closely monitored, limited in heir interaction with sensitive populations, and required to pay restitution to those whom they have wronged. The imprisonment of citizens should be undertaken with the strictest of scrutiny, as the incentives of prison operators and the mechanisms by which they are compensated are ripe for abuse.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: We oppose the use of red light cameras as a photo enforcement tool as well as any third party non law enforcement agency issuing fines of any kind.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: As individuals with rights to govern ourselves and our property, we support the ability to extend those rights to private security firms for the purposes of defending our life, liberty, and property.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: The power of arrest should be reserved to county sheriffs and their assigns. Outside agencies should be required to obtain permission from the sheriff prior to acting in the sheriff's jurisdiction.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: We oppose law enforcement “quotas” of any kind as a requirement or incentive in any law enforcement agency or activities.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: We oppose acceptance of federal funds by the State of Florida, or agencies thereof, which are earmarked for continuing the War on Drugs.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: Police roadblocks, Rights Free Zones, and searches without probable cause should be abolished. This includes U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s 100 Mile Border Zone which covers our State in its entirety.

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: 11. Pandemics and other Force Majeure Events

heading: IV. PUBLIC SAFETY
text: Government must never overstep its bounds, even in response to force majeure events, which include pandemics, natural disasters, and other crises. We condemn any misuse of authority by government to limit or restrict the rights of private property owners. We oppose all government restrictions on the transfer of information related to the event.

heading: V. VICE LAWS
text: Criminal sentencing should be reserved for crimes which have a discernible victim. The punishment should be appropriate to the crime. We oppose all laws and regulations that attempt to protect individuals from the consequences of their own behavior. While not necessarily condoning such activities, we advocate the repeal of all laws criminalizing gambling, possession and sale of drugs, and sexual relations between consenting adults. All those presently incarcerated or ever convicted solely for the commission of these victimless crimes must be pardoned and their records expunged.

heading: V. VICE LAWS
text: 2. Prohibitions by Private Organizations

heading: V. VICE LAWS
text: Private voluntary organizations, such as communities, clubs, unions, private universities or businesses may enforce rules that prohibit certain activities, such as gambling, prostitution, drug free or smoke free dorms.

heading: VI. Paying for Government
text: We advocate voluntary means of raising government revenues, such as user fees and donations, rather than taxation backed by force or threat of force. So long as citizens are coerced into funding government, we believe that government should accept payment in kind, in commodities, or in non fiat currencies.

heading: VI. Paying for Government
text: The State of Florida has levied enough taxes on its citizens and trade partners, as such, no new taxes ought to be levied for new government projects. New projects must be funded from existing revenues by reducing inefficiencies or cutting current spending.

heading: VI. Paying for Government
text: As long as we have taxes, equal protection of the law requires that for each type of tax, the rates should be the same and the tax base should be calculated in the same way for every individual or business. There should be no abatements, subsidies, credits, refunds or other preferential treatments as incentives to businesses to invest or create jobs, or as a privilege to individuals or classes of individuals, such as age, race or location. Such tax favoritism should be unconstitutional.

heading: VI. Paying for Government
text: Legislative budgeting of government has historically failed to control spending or the size of government. Therefore, we support amending the State Constitution to require a supermajority of the legislative houses to approve a total budget that exceeds that of the previous year and annual auditing of all funds spent made available by request as well as posted on State websites.

heading: VI. Paying for Government
text: In support of Localism, we prefer home rule as it is the most local jurisdiction of government, over ones more removed in State or Federal, as these entities largely consist of legislators from other jurisdictions.

heading: VII. Economy
text: We support free markets. We oppose all government laws or regulations, including but not limited to controls on prices, wages, rent, amounts sold, employment terms, ownership share terms, or other contractual terms, which interfere with private voluntary transactions. Ownership of property includes the right to transfer that property on any terms acceptable to all parties involved.

heading: VII. Economy
text: 2. Alternative Currencies and Legal Tender

heading: VII. Economy
text: The State shall not impose any regulations or restrictions on alternative currencies to the U.S. Dollar, nor shall it enforce legal tender laws.

heading: VII. Economy
text: We reject favoritism in any form to any industries, companies or other organizations. We oppose all grants, loans, loan guarantees and investments in business by any State or local government and all regulatory schemes that create privileges or disadvantages to any business or industry.

heading: VII. Economy
text: We call for abolishing all business and occupational licenses. The right of the people to conduct commerce is inherent, and should not require the permission of the State.

heading: VIII. Welfare and Charity
text: We support the right of private parties to provide charity and aid to those in need, and applaud court rulings correctly affirming First Amendment protection for that right. We condemn any effort by government to curtail or restrict private charity, and call for replacing government organizations and agencies which currently offer such aid and assistance with voluntary private efforts.

heading: IX. Education
text: 1. Parental Responsibility and Choice of Schools

heading: IX. Education
text: Because parents or guardians are best situated to decide what is in their own children’s best interests, it should be their right to decide their choice of school, type of school organization or homeschooling for them, and the responsibility of no one else to pay for it. Since the ultimate responsibility for the education of children rests with their parents, compulsory schooling and truancy laws must be repealed.

heading: IX. Education
text: 2. Civil Liberties in Government Education

heading: IX. Education
text: We oppose random drug tests and locker searches without probable cause, censorship of student publications or speeches, disarming of adults, school promotion of religion, suppression of student religious expressions, and other restrictions of civil liberties in government run schools .

heading: X. Environment
text: 1. Measures to Prevent Environmental Damage

heading: X. Environment
text: Protecting the environment requires a clear definition and enforcement of individual rights and responsibilities regarding resources like land, water, air, and wildlife. Oceans and waterways may not be deeded lands, but are to be protected and conserved similarly. Where damages can be proven and quantified in a court of law, restitution to the injured parties must be required. Immunity shall not be given to any industry, processor, or individual, related to damages occurring through these mediums, such as chemical run off. Other unowned mediums such as air, radio frequency, light, and sound should also be treated similarly when damages occur.

heading: X. Environment
text: Civil remedies are best pursued to make whole any victims.

heading: X. Environment
text: We look forward to the day when all property not required for police and court functions are returned to private ownership and control. Privatization of all public land not critical to government operations, may deed lock its future use for conservation or commercialization. We oppose the creation of new government parks or wilderness and recreation areas. Such parks and areas that already exist should be transferred to non government ownership. Pending such transfer, their operating costs should be borne by their users rather than by taxpayers.

heading: X. Environment
text: 3. State Withholding of Clean Energy Technology

heading: X. Environment
text: The withholding or prohibition of clean energy technologies by any government, military, or public entity, is viewed as equal to racketeering, and we oppose such manipulation of markets and such secrecy.

heading: XI. Health Care
text: The most fundamental property right is an individual’s right to own and control his or her own body. All individuals have the right to determine their own healthcare needs and treatment. Government should neither interfere nor impose upon the practitioner patient relationship.

heading: XI. Health Care
text: The right of people to extend or end their lives with dignity should not be infringed. We support the freedom to use living wills and durable medical powers of attorney.

heading: XI. Health Care
text: We support free choice for healthcare services, products and procedures, including the right to use experimental treatments.

heading: XI. Health Care
text: We favor free market regulation for all healthcare related matters, such as medication, providers, hospitals, insurance, testing, and the advocacy of same.

heading: XI. Health Care
text: 5. Medical Boards, Standards and Equipment

heading: XI. Health Care
text: We support voluntary medical boards and the free market establishment of industry standards and practices, and oppose government created barriers to entry. The manufacture of medication and medical equipment should not require approval by government.

heading: XII. Secession
text: We recognize secession as a political right that sovereigns reserve to sever any relationship which they voluntarily enter. The exercise of this right should not eliminate any legal or moral obligations to uphold the rights of others, including any debts owed.

heading: XII. Secession
text: We recognize and affirm that the sovereign State of Florida is in a voluntary relationship with the Union of States, and the sovereign individual is in a voluntary relationship with the State of Florida. We favor these entities, as they see fit, having regular and deliberative debate discerning the state of their union between them and larger bodies of government.

heading: XIII. INCLUSION
text: The Libertarian Party of Florida ratifies and hereby includes in this document the platform of the national Libertarian Party.

heading: XIV. OMISSIONS
text: Our silence about any other particular government law, regulation, ordinance, directive, edict, control, restriction, regulatory agency, activity, or objections should not be construed to imply approval.

heading: Why Libertarian
text: The Libertarian Party of Florida says you own your life. We agree. We will uphold and defend the Constitution, not just talk about it during campaign season. This campaign is for every Floridian. The smallest minority is the individual. That is who we serve.

heading: Your information. Our Policies.
text: This is a grassroots campaign website, not a store and not a government portal. If you write us, donate, volunteer, or ask for updates, we will treat that information like it belongs to you, and we will only use it to run this campaign and to follow Florida law.

heading: Who we are
text: This Privacy Policy covers scottjewett.com and the official online forms, emails, and pages used by Scott Jewett for Governor and Nicole Skelly for Lieutenant Governor (together, “the campaign,” “we,” or “us”).

heading: Who we are
text: Scott Jewett is the Libertarian candidate for Governor of Florida. Nicole Skelly is the Libertarian candidate for Lieutenant Governor. We trust people more than government. That includes how we handle the information you choose to give us.

heading: Who we are

heading: How we use it
text: Comply with law, respond to lawful requests, and protect the campaign, donors, volunteers, and the public.

heading: Florida campaign-finance reporting
text: This is a campaign for Governor and Lieutenant Governor of Florida. It is a state race. Donor reporting is governed by Chapter 106, Florida Statutes, and the Florida Division of Elections — not by a generic “business privacy” template.

heading: Florida campaign-finance reporting
text: Candidates must report contributions. Reports include the full name and address of each contributor. For contributions over $100, occupation is also reported. Those reports are public. If you donate above that threshold, your name, address, occupation, and amount can appear in public filings.

heading: Florida campaign-finance reporting
text: That is the tradeoff the law makes so people can see who funds campaigns. We will not pretend otherwise.

heading: Florida campaign-finance reporting
text: Cash contributions are limited by Florida law. Do not mail cash to the website. Use the official donate form or the instructions the campaign publishes.

text: We do not sell, rent, or lease your personal information to companies that want to pitch you a product.

heading: Who we share it with
text: Service vendors who run the site, process donations, send email, host forms, or provide analytics. They get only what they need to do that job. The Florida Division of Elections and other government offices when the law requires a report or a response.

heading: Who we share it with
text: The Libertarian Party of Florida or coordinated campaign work for this ticket, when sharing a volunteer or signup list actually helps elect Scott and Nicole.

heading: Who we share it with
text: Professional advisors such as a treasurer, compliance consultant, or lawyer bound to keep campaign records.

heading: Who we share it with
text: A successor campaign committee only if this committee is reorganized under the same ticket and Florida law allows the transfer.

heading: Who we share it with
text: We may also share information if you ask us to, or if we must do so to protect someone’s safety or to respond to a valid legal process.

heading: Email, updates, and texts
text: If you join Stay Informed or check an updates box, we will send campaign news, events, and asks. Every mass email will include a way to unsubscribe. You can also write us and ask to be removed from the list.

heading: Email, updates, and texts
text: Unsubscribing stops campaign updates. It does not erase a donation record we are required to keep, and it does not stop a receipt or a legally required notice.

heading: Email, updates, and texts
text: We will not sell your text opt-in, consent, or related mobile information to third parties. Vendors who actually send the texts are not a “sale.” Florida law has separate rules for political telephone and text ads, including “Paid for by” language on certain messages. We will follow those rules.

heading: Cookies and analytics
text: The site may use cookies and similar tools to:

heading: Cookies and analytics
text: Keep a page or form working (necessary cookies).

heading: Cookies and analytics
text: Remember a preference, such as a cookie banner choice.

heading: Cookies and analytics

heading: Cookies and analytics
text: You can block non-essential cookies in your browser. The site may work less smoothly if you do. We do not use your visit to this site to build a commercial advertising profile to sell to other businesses.

heading: Cookies and analytics
text: If we use a tool such as Google Analytics, it is to understand whether the site is doing its job — not to run a retail storefront.

heading: Your choices
text: Read the site without submitting a form.

heading: Your choices
text: Give us only the fields a form requires.

heading: Your choices
text: Ask us to correct a name, email, or address we use to contact you.

heading: Your choices
text: Ask what campaign-contact information we have on you, subject to the records we must keep under Florida law.

heading: Your choices
text: We may not delete a donation record, occupation field, or other data that campaign-finance law requires us to keep and report. We can stop using your email for updates.

heading: Your choices
text: To make a request, use the Contact page or email [INSERT CAMPAIGN EMAIL] with “Privacy request” in the subject line. We will verify that the request is really from you before changing a record.

heading: Your choices
text: Some states have consumer privacy statutes written for businesses that sell data. This committee is a political campaign. We do not sell personal information for money. We do not use this website as a commercial store.

heading: Your choices
text: If a law still gives you a right we can honor without breaking Florida campaign-finance rules, write us and we will handle it in good faith. Campaign-finance reports already filed cannot be unpublished by a website form.

heading: Your choices
text: We use reasonable safeguards — encrypted connections on the site, limited staff access, and vendors who are supposed to protect payment data. No website is perfectly safe. Do not send Social Security numbers, passwords, or extra financial details by ordinary email.

heading: Your choices
text: We keep information as long as the campaign needs it to communicate, comply with law, handle disputes, and close out the committee. Florida record-retention rules for campaign reports apply even after Election Day.

heading: Children
text: This site is for adults who can vote, donate, and volunteer. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If a parent believes a child submitted a form, write us and we will delete what the law allows us to delete.

heading: Children
text: The site may link to donation processors, social networks, the Libertarian Party of Florida, news stories, or government pages. Those sites have their own rules. Read theirs before you submit information there.

heading: Changes
text: If we change this policy, we will post the new version on this page with a new date. If the change is material, we may also note it by email or a site banner. Keep using the site after an update only if you accept the new policy.

heading: How to reach us
text: This website is a political campaign site for Scott Jewett for Governor and Nicole Skelly for Lieutenant Governor. Content is campaign speech and general information. It is not legal, tax, insurance, or medical advice. It is not a government service.

heading: How to reach us
text: Do not break the law on this site. Do not try to hack it, scrape it at scale, plant malware, harvest emails, impersonate the campaign, or interfere with donations and forms. We can block access if you abuse the site.

heading: How to reach us
text: If you send comments, photos, volunteer stories, or testimonials, you give the campaign permission to use them to run this race — on the site, in email, and in ads — unless you tell us in writing that a specific item is private.

heading: How to reach us
text: Campaign text, design, logos, and video belong to the campaign or to people who licensed them to us. You may share pages and quote short passages with credit. Do not copy the site as if it were yours.

heading: How to reach us
text: Contributions are not tax-deductible. Florida law governs who may give and what must be reported. By donating, you confirm you are using your own lawful funds and the information on the form is true. A donation supports the campaign. It does not buy access, a favor, or a job.
